admission.justification: Realized in the kernel vocabulary module, which refuses removed members by name, in the contract reader, which keeps old cells readable, and in the disabled-memory classifiers; the vocabulary and boundary tests guard the removal.

applicability: Every place the product names, reads or refuses a memory mode.
conditions: The member is disabled or another removed mode.
exclusions: Unknown tokens, which stay invalid requests, and the removed internal mode, which keeps its own refusal first.

evidence: requirements/MIK-R50-v1-a-task-cannot-opt-out-of-memory-where-knowledge-exists.md rules 1-2; mcp/tests/test_memory_mode_removal.py: 44 function definitions, 59 collected node IDs (42 plain + 13 corrected-surface rows + 4 lookalike rows; collect-identities receipt SHA256:253d4bbdcfdcf65747935785edc2e3eeed2038592bd423c42ec0adc3f50bd91e); mcp/tests/test_wire_vocabulary_exhaustiveness_boundary.py (unknown-cell reading). An earlier '(57 converted cases)' figure in this evidence string matched no receipt and is struck.

statement: The disabled memory mode is removed from the product vocabulary: only external starts; an empty or unknown stored cell with no recorded worktree or ledger still reads as disabled so old contracts stay legible, while a section showing either reads external.
